The lowest common ancestor of Etoricoxib and Celecoxib is identified as an Organonitrogen Heterocyclic Compound, a class of compounds that includes Cyclooxygenase Inhibitors, which are known to interact with Mapk14. This suggests that Etoricoxib may share a common mechanism of action with Celecoxib, potentially through a shared interaction with Mapk14. The evidence points to a possible dependency on Mapk14 in the context of these interactions, though the exact nature of the relationship remains to be fully elucidated.
